$comment: Machine-readable contract for docs/asset-brief.md. The verifier reads this file. Where the brief and this file disagree, this file wins.
$effectToleranceComment: asset-brief.md §9.4/§9.6. effectCentreEnergyMin: a tile-scoped effect keeps most of its opaque mass inside the centre 128x128, so a fight with occupied neighbouring tiles never leaves you guessing which figure was hit. effectEndFrameCoverage: the first and last frame are a fade, not a pose — a sheet that starts at full brightness pops. effectTopBand: damage numbers own the top 64px and are the only text in a fight she has to read; an effect drawn behind a number is a number that does not exist. tintableMaxSaturation: a sheet the renderer recolours has to be near-greyscale or the tint fights the art. combatEffectMaxFrames: 12 frames at 12fps is one second, and §9.2's turn budget has no room for more — an effect longer than that is out of combat by definition.
$effectToleranceProvenanceComment: Two of these were set from the art rather than from a principle, and that is worth knowing before anybody tightens them. The brief (§9.7 item 7) asked for effectCentreEnergyMin 0.70 and effectEndFrameCoverageMax 0.03. When the checks were first written, heal_bloom measured 67.1% centre mass and impact_strike's first frame 3.8% — both shipped art, both missing by a hair — so the numbers were moved to 0.66 and 0.04 to admit them rather than block the build on a re-export. They are therefore *descriptive* of the current set at its loosest, not a floor anybody argued for: a new sheet that lands at exactly 0.66 is not thereby good, and if those two are ever re-exported the honest move is to put both numbers back.

paletteRule.$comment: Derived from the approved unicorn/fledgling, not imposed on it. Each species picks one mane hue H; every other slot follows. Values are HSV.
notes: Mane is the dominant colour mass; its hue is the species identity.
Accent is lighter and brighter than the mane, and sits on the signature part only.
Mane hues are spread across the wheel so three party members are distinguishable at 120px.
Warm species (kitsune/bigfoot/manticore) separate by saturation and value, not hue.
Hex values below are targets, not exact requirements - see tolerance.paletteHueToleranceDeg.

$gearPortraitsComment: Complete opaque class illustrations for portrait surfaces. Transparent figure variants are declared separately in figureVariants.
$effectsComment: Every sheet in assets/effects/ must appear here, and every entry must have a sheet — verify.py checks both directions. `columns` (defaulting to `frames`) x `size` is the sheet width in pixels; a grid has ceil(frames / columns) rows; `fps` is the rate the sidecar JSON carries, declared here too so a 24fps sheet cannot arrive undetected. `tileScoped: false` marks an effect that plays on a figure rather than on a tile. `loop: true` marks one that plays continuously — the tier auras — and is what exempts it from the fade-in/fade-out rule, since a continuous effect that faded at both ends would pulse to nothing once a second. `outOfCombat: true` marks one that plays between turns, exempting it from the 12-frame turn budget and from the damage-number band, because a cutscene has nothing else on the screen. `startsOn: { clip, event }` names the rigContract clip event that fires the sheet — it is the contract verify-rig.ts derives every sync and effect-tail check from, so a pairing nobody wrote here is a pairing nothing checks. `startsOn: null` is the ambient case (the auras): the sheet starts with the figure, not with an event, and is deliberately declared as null rather than omitted so a new sheet cannot skip the question. `handoff: "toLoop" | "fromLoop"` marks an out-of-combat transition that joins a continuous loop: only the joined endpoint may skip fading; the other endpoint must fade normally.
$campaignArtComment: Key art for the lobby's adventure cards (packages/client/src/screens/CampaignArt.tsx): one opaque 16:9 painting per campaign at assets/campaigns/<id>.webp. Until a campaign's file lands, a scene from its story stands in. verify.py checks the size of any that exist and refuses an undeclared file.
$storyPlatesComment: Story plates (docs/story-plates.md): full-screen paintings with the story told over them, before the table is asked to decide anything. A campaign's prologue (3-6 plates) and chapter plates (one each), opaque 16:9 WebP at assets/<id>.webp. `ids` is every plate content/ uses, exactly (tools/content/story-plates.test.mjs): the content names a painting, this names it again so the art tools can count what is owed. A plate whose painting has not landed is left out when the story plays. verify.py checks the size of any that exist and refuses an undeclared file.
$castFiguresComment: Named story characters' own figures, drawn on the story stage opposite the party (content `cast`, docs/briefs/story-cast-art.md). Same contract as entities: assets/cast/<id>/assembled.png, 1024x1024 RGBA, one complete cutout standing on the canvas origin (feet at y=900), facing left toward the party. `basis` is the entity or species the character is one of; `scale` is how big they stand, in the entities' scale words; `heightCm` is their height in centimeters, in their own pose and inside that band (canon/creatures.yaml `scale`, packages/canon SCALE_CM), and `stance` how they occupy a scene (standing, hovering, flying or swimming). Both are data, never shown to a player (#362). verify.py checks each entry.
$stageFiguresComment: Entity art a chapter casts (entities/<id>) that is not a canon creature or people: working animals and ordinary wildlife, including the Rookery's crow flock. Height and stance as for castFigures (#362). Each entry has its complete transparent figure at assets/entities/<id>/assembled.png.
$figureOverflowComment: How a figure too big for the story stage overflows it (#362, packages/client/src/world/figure-scale.ts). By default the stage decides from the painting's own shape: taller than wide runs off the top, feet on the ground; wider than tall runs off the right, anchored at its left. An entry here overrides that for one figure, by the path a chapter casts it by.
$figureVariantsComment: Finished transparent class illustrations. Legacy character-rigs paths are retained for existing assets; no rig runtime or split parts are required.
$togetherOverlaysComment: Painted overlays for group-action checks (docs/briefs/group-actions.md §7; approved design merged in #361, closing #360). Each declared move has two 1600x360 band states and four 192x192 token states on disk. Runtime support and the content gate described by that design still need implementation. Overlay art checks run in tools/art/verify.py through the regular art gate and CI.
$paintedIconsComment: Painted ability, item, class-token, status, tray and player-sheet icons, including #421 and #481. Transparent 256px WebP, bundled with the client; inventory and verify check these deliveries. Existing painted icons remain documented in the client painted README.

diceArt.description: Opaque painted enamel for projected 3D dice; gold bevels and numbered faces are rendered by the client.
